It's the primary output format for **GFS, HRRR, NBM, GEFS, NAM**, and similar numerical weather prediction products.\n56\t\n57\tDecoding it means handling multi-section message framing, four grid geometries, parameter tables indexed by discipline/category/number, five data-packing algorithms, and bitmaps for missing-value masking.\n58\t\n59\tThe standard tools (`wgrib2`, `eccodes`) are C programs. If you need decoded GRIB2 values in a Rust project, your options were: shell out, bind through FFI, or give up and parse bytes yourself.\n60\t\n61\t**gribtract is the native Rust alternative.**\n62\t\n63\t## ✨ Features\n64\t\n65\t- 🦀 **Pure Rust core** — no C toolchain or FFI for simple, complex, complex+spatial-differencing, and PNG packing (DRT 5.0 / 5.2 / 5.3 / 5.41); JPEG2000 (5.40) available behind the optional `jpeg2000` feature\n66\t- 🏷️ **Typed output** — every decoded field carries structured metadata: parameter ID, level, forecast time, grid geometry\n67\t- 🗺️ **Four grid projections** — lat/lon (GDT 3.0), polar stereographic (3.20), Lambert conformal (3.30), Gaussian (3.40)\n68\t- ⚡ **Lazy decode path** — parse headers only, defer grid data; extract single grid points in **O(1)** for DRT=0 fields without decoding the full grid\n69\t- 📈 **Timeseries extractor** — pull per-station forecast series for a list of lat/lon coordinates in one call\n70\t- 🌐 **Byte-range fetching** — `gribtract-fetch` downloads GRIB2 (or slices of it) from NOAA S3, GCS, and NOMADS over HTTP range requests\n71\t- 🐍 **Python bindings** — `gribtract-py` (PyO3) exposes the decoder to Python\n72\t- ✅ **Oracle-gated correctness** — every release is verified against eccodes/wgrib2 over a corpus of real NOAA files; agreement can only ratchet up\n73\t\n74\t## 📦 Crate Layout\n75\t\n76\t```\n77\tgribtract/\n78\t├── crates/\n79\t│   ├── gribtract-core      # 🔩 Section parser, template decoders, unpacking. random access isn't possible. The recommended pattern is **decode once, extract many**:\n\n```rust\nuse gribtract::{decode_lazy, decode_all_drt3};\n\nlet lazy_fields = gribtract::decode_lazy(&bytes)?;\nfor lf in &lazy_fields {\n    if let (Some(body), Some(extra)) = (&lf.section7_raw, &lf.complex_extra) {\n        let n = lf.grid.num_data_points as usize;\n        let grid: Vec<f64> = decode_all_drt3(body, &lf.packing, extra, n)?;\n\n        // Now extract any number of stations by index, O(1) each\n        for (lat, lon) in &station_coords {\n            let idx = lf.grid.nearest_index(*lat, *lon)?;\n            println!(\"value: {}\", grid[idx]);\n        }\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### 🐍 Python\n\n```bash\npip install maturin\nmaturin develop -p gribtract-py\n```\n\n```python\nimport gribtract\n\nfields = gribtract.decode(open(\"hrrr.t00z.wrfsfcf01.grib2\", \"rb\").read())\nfor f in fields:\n    print(f.parameter, f.level, f.forecast_hour)\n```\n\n## 🔬 The Correctness Oracle\n\ngribtract is built **oracle-first**: correctness is defined as agreement with eccodes/wgrib2 over real files, not as passing hand-written unit tests.\n\n```\ngribtract decode  ─┐\n                   ├─→ compare field-by-field + grid values within derived tolerance\neccodes/wgrib2    ─┘\n```\n\nThe differential harness in `gribtract-testutil` runs both decoders over a corpus of real NOAA GRIB2 files (GFS, HRRR, NBM, GEFS) and compares:\n\n- **Metadata exactly** — center, parameter ID, level, forecast time, grid geometry\n- **Grid values within derived tolerance** — computed from the packing template's own scale factors, never an arbitrary epsilon\n\nAny disagreement becomes a permanent regression fixture. The agreement percentage can only increase; there is no mechanism to silently drop a covered template.\n\n```bash\n# Run the differential tests\ncargo test -p gribtract -- differential\n\n# Fetch and verify against the full corpus (requires eccodes installed)\ncargo xtask corpus fetch\ncargo xtask corpus verify\n```\n\n## 📊 Performance Dashboard\n\nA self-contained benchmark dashboard (`dashboard.html`) tracks decode throughput on real NOAA files, fed by `bench-results.json`. Speed numbers are never reported without a corresponding correctness verification run.\n\n```bash\ncargo xtask bench    # run benchmarks, regenerate bench-results.json\ncargo xtask serve    # serve the live dashboard with streaming updates\n```\n\n## 🏗️ Building from Source\n\nRequires **Rust 1.75+**.\n\n```bash\ngit clone https://github.com/jedarden/gribtract\ncd gribtract\ncargo build --release\n```\n\nThe `gribtract-py` extension is excluded from the default workspace build (it needs Python headers for PyO3) — build it explicitly with `maturin develop -p gribtract-py`.\n\n## 💻 CLI Reference\n\n> **⚠️ Not yet implemented** — The CLI commands below are documented for the planned interface, but are not yet functional.
